editorial_changes: Proposition 1.3.1 proves existence first and names each following proof goal. It specifies every crucial g,z,v,w substitution, expands real bilinearity in the basis 1,i, defines the variable point ζ and scalar α, and explains transport by s(z).
Definition 1.3.2 derives speed and path length from ds². Proposition 1.3.3 separates tangent, length, distance and area arguments and expands the Jacobian cancellation.

Theorem 1.3.4 begins with the full length integral, solves explicitly for the real circle center, describes its perpendicular-bisector construction, straightens the circle by a Möbius transformation, computes the inverse, and transfers both minimizing arcs and distance from the vertical case. The final invariant-ratio calculation returns to the original points.

A mathematical vector diagram shows the same circle and its exact vertical image, with matching endpoints, center, equal radii, perpendicular bisector and caption. It is explanatory artwork, not proof evidence.

The height example retains its length computations without unexplained cusp/horocycle terms. Horocycles are introduced with cusps in Section 1.7. The stronger Radon discussion is now situated in Section 1.8 with Haar measure.
Gradient is derived from metric duality; divergence is derived from the first variation of the area density under a local deformation and characterized by integration against test functions.

Definition 1.3.6 defines Δ as -div grad and derives the coordinate cancellation. Theorem 1.3.7 proves commutation with smooth Riemannian isometries, including orientation reversal, through gradient transport, area preservation and divergence transport.
Proposition 1.3.8 proves the Green identity, symmetry and nonnegativity on compactly supported smooth functions. Self-adjoint domains and quotient operators are explicitly deferred to Chapter 11.
Retained labels and numbers 1.3.1–1.3.6 are preserved. The notational index now has 65 entries, adding gradient and divergence and clarifying the Laplacian convention.

proof_correspondence: The candidate tangent form is an actual real bilinear form, not only a numerical formula or a premise asserting the conclusion. Its invariance uses the complex pairing scaling identity and the previously proved derivative and imaginary-part formulas.
Unsquared tangent invariance follows from equality of squares and nonnegativity. Path differentiation and integration are distinct remaining steps.
Gradient duality proves equality against every real tangent vector for an arbitrary real linear differential. It does not yet formalize the differential of a C¹ function as a smooth vector field.
The two-point ratio uses the same denominator cancellation as the expanded prose; no distance is defined by this invariant to bypass the path-length target.
Previously recorded uniqueness, positive-density and Section 1.1–1.2 proof-route differences remain in the section comparisons.
